issues.legal_issue: A notified-area decision must be based on consideration of the statutory eligibility conditions for the area.
material_facts: The challenged notification included portions of villages described as rural and inhabited by agriculturists.
The applicable statute required a notified area to contain a town or bazaar and not to be a purely agricultural village.
Whether the shops and bus traffic in the area amounted to a bazaar or established a town was disputed.
The Court examined the administrative record and found no apparent consideration of whether the statutory conditions were satisfied.
issues.conclusion: The record did not show that the State Government considered the statutory eligibility conditions before making the designation, so the decision could not stand without that determination.
issues.legal_principle: Section 256 of the Himachal Pradesh Municipal Act, 1968 permits designation only subject to the statutory conditions, including that the area contain a town or bazaar and not be a purely agricultural village. The State Government must consider whether those conditions are met before making the administrative decision.

predicates.challenge_to_notified_area_decision: A party challenged an administrative decision designating an area as a notified area.
predicates.statutory_eligibility_conditions_apply: The governing enactment made designation conditional on the area containing a town or bazaar and not being purely agricultural.
predicates.administrative_record_lacked_considerati: The administrative record did not show that the decision-maker assessed whether the statutory eligibility conditions were satisfied.
predicates.designation_is_unsustainable: The designation cannot stand because the required eligibility conditions were not shown to have been considered.

issues.definition: When a challenged notified-area decision is subject to statutory eligibility conditions and the administrative record shows no consideration of them, the designation is unsustainable.

issues.legal_issue: Residents must be given a fair opportunity to be heard before an administrative decision exposes them to civil consequences, unless the law excludes natural justice.
material_facts: The notification removed the affected areas from the jurisdiction of existing Gram Panchayats, causing elected representatives to cease holding office in respect of those areas.
The change would subject residents to higher taxes and a change from an agricultural to a semi-urban way of life.
The residents were not given an opportunity to present their views before the notification was made.
The statute made no provision expressly excluding an opportunity to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The residents had to be given an opportunity to be heard before the notified area was constituted; a fair process of inviting and considering objections was sufficient, and an oral hearing was not required.
issues.legal_principle: Where administrative action entails civil consequences, natural justice applies unless the law excludes it. The Court relied on S.L. Kapoor v. Jagmohan and State of Orissa v. Sridhar Kumar Mallik. Although Section 256 of the Himachal Pradesh Municipal Act, 1968 did not expressly provide for a hearing, it did not exclude natural justice; the opportunity may be provided through written objections that are fairly considered.

predicates.challenge_to_notified_area_decision: A party challenged an administrative decision designating an area as a notified area.
predicates.designation_caused_civil_consequences: The designation affected residents' local representation, tax burden, or way of life.
predicates.law_did_not_exclude_natural_justice: The governing law did not expressly exclude a fair opportunity for affected residents to present their views.
predicates.residents_must_receive_a_fair_opportunit: Affected residents must be given a fair opportunity to present their views before the designation is made.

issues.definition: When a challenged notified-area designation causes civil consequences and the law does not exclude natural justice, residents must receive a fair opportunity to be heard.
